That paper is of surface voids, not internal voids. Surface voids can also improve aerodynamics (example, see golf balls). Voids are frequently negative for a variety of reasons. One of which is they can unexpectedly transfer loads though the part which in turn are attempting to transfer/share loads elsewhere. Others can change attributes such as ductility, sheering, and compressibility.

Please see section, 3.3. Stress concentrations. This is the exactly problem I'm talking about. Voids create surfaces. It's those surfaces allow stresses to be transfered around the void. Here, everything has an adjacent void. Meaning, it's more likely to ultimately transfer all the stress to the weakest bonds or fractures within the part. Yet this manufacturing process, in of itself, insures the object is never actually solid. The cooking process is to reduce internal tensions and create crystallization, strengthening the parts.
